newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Anwar warns against listing violations.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Anwar warns against listing violations.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday warned companies seeking to list their stock that regulators would not tolerate any violations of securities laws.

In a speech prepared for delivery to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's (KLSE) annual dinner, Anwar said: "I commend the Securities Commission for its firm decision in withdrawing the listing approval to Fumakilla."
"Let this be a lesson and deterrent to other companies seeking to list on the KLSE. We will not hesitate to take action those who flout the rules and regulations," Anwar added.
Market regulator, the Securities Commission, on November 28 revoked its approval to allow the listing of Fumakilla Malaysia Bhd, a maker of household insecticide products.
The commission said the company made misleading statements to the regulator, including on its Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) shareholding.
Under a government policy, all publicly listed companies should have at least 30 percent of their equity held by Bumiputras.
"I must caution that we don't intend to tolerate this," Anwar said referring to the violations involving Bumiputra representation in new listing.
He also delivered a sharply worded rebuke to the Malaysian stockbroking industry.

He said among other things that the results of a survey jointly conducted by the commission and the KLSE found the quality of local stockbroking research was not up to standard and there was lack of training at the firms.
Anwar said he found the survey results "unfortunately rather appalling".
He said by the end of the century, between 200 and 300 companies are expected to be added on to the KLSE which already has 600 listed.
